poster_title: Seeing, Listening, Remembering, and Reasoning: A Multimodal Agent with Long-Term Memory
authors: Lin Long, Yichen He, Wentao Ye, Yiyuan Pan, Yuan Lin, Hang Li, Junbo Zhao, Wei Li
paper_info: Date: October 10, 2025; Correspondence: linyuan.0@bytedance.com; Project Page: https://m3-agent.github.io

panels.headline: Continuous perception and long-term memory are essential for intelligent agents to perform complex tasks.
content: Existing multimodal agents often focus on low-level visual details.
This leads to ambiguity and inconsistency in long-term contexts.
M3-Agent aims to address these issues with a novel framework.
It integrates real-time visual and auditory processing with long-term memory.
The goal is to enhance the agent's ability to construct and maintain coherent world knowledge.

panels.headline: Handling infinite information processing in real-time multimodal streams.
content: Real-time processing of multimodal data is challenging.
Agents must construct coherent and consistent world knowledge.
This is particularly difficult in highly dynamic environments.
The paper proposes solutions to these challenges.
It introduces a new benchmark for evaluating these capabilities.

panels.headline: M3-Agent continuously processes real-time visual and auditory inputs to construct and update episodic and semantic memories.
content: Episodic memory captures concrete events.
Semantic memory extracts general knowledge from the environment.
Memory is organized in an entity-centric structure.
This enables consistent and coherent long-term knowledge.
The system consists of two parallel processes: memorization and control.
panels.figure_caption: Architecture of M3-Agent, comprising a multimodal large language model (MLLM) and a multimodal long-term memory.

panels.headline: M3-Agent outperforms the strongest baseline, Gemini-GPT4o-Hybrid, by 6.7%, 7.7%, and 5.3% on M3-Bench-robot, M3-Bench-web, and VideoMME-long, respectively.
content: Two benchmarks: M3-Bench-robot (100 videos) and M3-Bench-web (920 videos).
M3-Bench-robot features long videos from realistic robotic work scenarios.
M3-Bench-web expands video diversity for broader evaluation.
Ablation study shows significant performance drops when removing semantic memory.
Results demonstrate superior performance across multiple benchmarks.
panels.figure_caption: Results on M3-Bench-robot, M3-Bench-web, and VideoMME-long, comparing M3-Agent with other methods.

panels.headline: Removing semantic memory reduces accuracy by 17.1%, 19.2%, and 13.1% on M3-Bench-robot, M3-Bench-web, and VideoMME-long, respectively.
content: Semantic memory is crucial for performance.
Ablation studies highlight the importance of each component.
DAPO training algorithm outperforms GRPO.
Performance gains from DAPO scale with model size.
Removing inter-turn instruction and reasoning negatively impacts performance.
panels.figure_caption: Impact of different memorization models on final performance.

panels.headline: M3-Agent advances multimodal agents toward more human-like long-term memory and reasoning capabilities.
content: M3-Agent introduces a novel multimodal agent framework with long-term memory.
It develops M3-Bench, a new LVQA benchmark for evaluating memory and reasoning.
The framework demonstrates superior performance across multiple benchmarks.
It provides valuable insights for the practical design of intelligent agents.
Future work will focus on improving long-term consistency in dynamic environments.
